name: Sonar Sweep
summary: A calm scope whose conic beam never stops turning: metrics are blips, and one pings back coral so a human can decide.
look: Deep teal-black glass with range rings labelled by metric, bearing ticks and faint scanlines. A conic-gradient beam with a phosphor tail rotates forever, blips glow and fade behind it, and the anomaly announces itself with coral ping rings and a slide-up contact card.

components.name: Scope + range rings
components.role: concentric rings labelled by metric; the whole product surface in one circle

components.name: Conic sweep
components.role: CSS conic-gradient beam with phosphor tail; the always-on background watcher

components.name: Blips
components.role: metric dots whose alpha decays after each pass; healthy signals

components.name: Ping rings
components.role: three coral expanding circles; the anomaly announcing itself

components.name: Contact card
components.role: 'Contact 07 · locked' card with metric, context and Roll back / Acknowledge

components.name: Bearing strip
components.role: mono readouts (bearing, clock, metric count) around the scope

motion.name: Sweep
motion.how: linear 360° per 2 bars (4 s at 120 BPM), never eased; the film's metronome

motion.name: Blip decay
motion.how: each blip 1 → 0.15 opacity over one rotation, triggered by its angle as the beam crosses

motion.name: Ping
motion.how: ring scale 0 → 3, opacity 1 → 0, power2.out; three staggered rings on three kicks

story: Hook: a dead scope at 03:14, sweep off, grey blips flickering unseen: '38 dashboards. Nobody watching.' Reveal: on the drop the beam ignites from the Acme mark at the hub and starts turning; 'Acme Pulse' rises beneath. Proof: the beam turns across rings labelled Signups, Active users, p95 latency and Checkout; one blip pings coral, the scope locks and a card slides up: 'Contact 07 · Checkout conversion −18% · since 09:42 · after deploy #2231' with Roll back. CTA: the scope fills the frame behind 'You ship. Pulse watches.' and Start free.
adapt: Label the rings with your own objects (services, regions, customers, pipelines) and let the contact card show your product's real alert and action.

fit.risk: Radar carries military connotations; keep it calm and scientific, with no crosshairs or targeting language.
